questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if there is no traffic nearby.
Signal only if you see other traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if there is no traffic nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you turn, change lanes, or pull away from the curb. Do not skip signaling just because you do not see other cars. Make signaling a habit.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains cross first.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains cross first.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach railroad tracks. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Do not make any driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their cars.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your car out of traffic if you can. Stay out of traffic lanes so other cars do not hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Taking amphetamines.
Being angry.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.explanation: Tiredness and alcohol affect your driving the same way. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you about as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight affects you like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to your exit.
Flag down a police officer to help you back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop on the highway, back up, make sudden lane changes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing the street illegally in the middle instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always stop for pedestrians. Even if they are jaywalking or crossing where they should not, you must still let them pass.

questions.question: When you see this road sign, you should:

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign means a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign tells you to keep right to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
Drivers always check their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers give the right-of-way to others.
Drivers keep a four-second distance between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers speed. Always follow speed limits and drive slower when conditions are bad.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas where your vision blurs when you are tired.
Areas next to your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas next to your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check the areas near the back corners of your vehicle. You cannot see these areas in your mirrors. They are called blind spots.

questions.question: When should you let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if the pedestrians are not using their phones.
Always.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians pass. You can only move forward if your lane is completely clear and no one is crossing.

questions.question: It starts to sleet or snow while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clean.
Stay farther back from the car in front of you.
Be careful when passing other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead. Roads are slippery, and you need more distance to stop.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol at a social event, what is the safest way to drive home?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Wait 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to stay safe is to get a ride from a sober friend. Drinking coffee or taking a cold shower does not reduce alcohol in your body. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Since driving involves risks, you should always work to improve your driving and awareness skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe when drivers think they have nothing to learn. Always try to improve your driving and awareness skills to keep yourself and others safe.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking lot or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when pulling from a parking space into traffic, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: In the District of Columbia, can your driver license be revoked for a drug offense that is not related to driving?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: In the District of Columbia, your driver license can be revoked if you are convicted of a drug offense, even if it has nothing to do with driving.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see if anyone is in your blind spot. Do all of these things before you move.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely.
Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden under the seat.
To stop the seat belt alarm.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with enough room to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What does a "Merging lanes" sign tell you?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times when driving.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you cannot drive safely. Stress reduces your concentration. It is better to wait to drive than to drive when you are upset.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass on a hill or curve, at an intersection, or near a railroad crossing. Never pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a multilane road with a median or center turn lane.

questions.question: Night driving can be more difficult than driving during the day because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far or as clearly. Always use your headlights. Drive slow enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
Stop and back up.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway or shoulder is illegal.
